chapter: Streetcar, Cab revival shows and trips abroad
title: Acting in 'Angel in the Pawn Shop' as a clarinetist
summary: He was rejected for the Broadway original for being bald, then won raves in the 1960 Philadelphia summer stock production.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Now, then when I got back to New York, what's this -- oh, I came back to New York, and I became an actor, and I did the play, Angel in the Pawn Shop with -- in fact, I was the original Angel in the Pawn Shop opened on Broadway right after I finished Streetcar Named Desire, and I made a reading for it, and they didn't hire me because I was bald-headed. It was just -- the story was about a clarinet player that came into a pawn shop to pawn his clarinet under the condition that the

pawn shop owner would let him come and practice every day, and it finally ended up where he was in there practicing -- the girl there talked the pawn shop broker into letting him do this. And at the end of the picture some robbers came in and robbed the pawn shop, and the clarinet player conked them on the head with the clarinet, you know.

But it was a pretty good show. Anyway, I was -- I didn't get the original show. Willie Lewis got it. Remember Willie Lewis? Clarinet player -- well, he got it, and he was almost as bald as I, but he wasn't the clarinet player that I was, you know, but he got it.

And so when they had the -- in 1960, they didn't hired me because I was bald -- so now in 1960 when they got ready to do this Angel in the Pawn Shop in summer stock in Philly at the Theater In the Round, they called me, and I did it, and I was the only one that got raving notices, you know.
